extracted.intended_audience: researchers, organizations, small businesses, and individuals seeking to submit Solution Summaries or proposals to ARPA‑H solicitations
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and submitting Solution Summaries and proposals to ARPA‑H solicitations (Innovative Solution Openings/ISOs), including eligibility, registration, teaming, evaluation, budgeting, IP, and performance/milestone expectations. Focused on complying with solicitation-specific requirements and ARPA‑H procedural norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovative Solution Opening (ISO) definition and use
rubrics_metrics.description: An ISO is a unique solicitation instrument created by ARPA-H to make awards for most of its R&D efforts. ISOs are not bound by the Federal Acquisition Regulations like Broad Agency Announcements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ISOs can be Program‑Specific ISOs or Mission Office ISOs and are referred to more generally as solicitations. Understand which ISO type a solicitation is (Program‑Specific vs Mission Office) because it affects submission expectations and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program‑Specific ISO vs Mission Office ISO differences
rubrics_metrics.description: A Program‑Specific ISO is used to solicit potential solutions for a specific ARPA‑H program. A Mission Office ISO is used to solicit and fund individual research projects that align with ARPA‑H's areas of interest but fall outside any specific ARPA‑H Program or Initiative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program‑Specific ISOs are program‑driven; Mission Office ISOs may have limited funding and ARPA‑H’s submission reviews may take longer. Mission Office ISOs are open for multiple years and involve rolling submissions and typically do not have Proposers’ Day events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programs vs Initiatives distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs are a collective set of research projects managed by a Program Manager focused on a specific problem. Initiatives are special efforts designed to rapidly move from proposal to funded contracts, and may include sprints and unique funding tracks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect different timelines and structures—initiatives move faster and may follow unique funding tracks; programs align with broader R&D goals and are managed centrally by a Program Manager.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding instrument: Other Transactions (OT) rather than grants
rubrics_metrics.description: ARPA‑H is not a grant‑making agency. ARPA‑H primarily uses Other Transactions research and development (R&D) efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OTs are often performance‑based agreements where funding is contingent on meeting aggressive milestones and performance criteria agreed during award negotiations. OTs allow Program Manager involvement throughout the effort, and generally provide more flexibility (including IP flexibility) than financial assistance regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — who may apply
rubrics_metrics.description: All responsible sources capable of satisfying the government’s needs: academia, non‑profit organizations, for‑profit entities, hospitals, community health centers, non‑federal research centers, researchers, and individuals capable of performing research and/or development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small businesses are welcome; confirm eligibility details in each solicitation. Review solicitation‑specific eligibility and requirements carefully before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small business (SBIR/STTR) eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: ARPA‑H will announce SBIR and STTR award opportunities; only small businesses are eligible to submit proposals to these solicitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ARPA‑H defines a small business according to SBA guidelines and federal regulations. Eligibility criteria vary slightly between SBIR and STTR — confirm all criteria in the solicitation before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑U.S. organizations and foreign entity limits
rubrics_metrics.description: ARPA‑H can directly fund a foreign entity; however, ARPA‑H will prioritize awards to entities that conduct funded work in the U.S. Awards will not be made to entities organized under the laws of a covered foreign country (Russia, Iran, North Korea, China).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each solicitation defines eligibility and requirements for international entities. See International Affairs FAQs for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission platform and registration requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise indicated, proposers will submit Solution Summaries and proposals to the ARPA‑H Solutions site, ARPA‑H's custom submission and registration platform. Registration and log‑in are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start by reading solicitation documents for exact instructions. Use the 'Ask A Question' feature on the Solutions site for opportunity‑specific queries (sign‑in required).

rubrics_metrics.name: SAM.gov and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All ARPA‑H solicitations require a valid UEI at the time of proposal submission. Prior to award, all proposers must complete registration in SAM.gov and maintain active status throughout the life of the award. Some solicitations may require an active SAM.gov registration at the time of proposal submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan early — UEI can take 1–3 business days typically; full SAM.gov registration can take 7–10 business days and full approval 2–6 weeks depending on complexity. Read the solicitation for specific timing. Beware of third‑party services that charge for SAM.gov registration; SAM.gov is free.

rubrics_metrics.name: UEI and SAM nuances for pre‑proposal steps and subcontractors
rubrics_metrics.description: UEI requirements for Solution Summaries and pre‑proposal submissions vary by solicitation. Subcontractors and teaming partners are not typically required to have a UEI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposers are encouraged to begin SAM.gov registration even if UEI is not required at Solution Summary stage. If a non‑registered team member later becomes the lead or requires direct payment, that entity will need active SAM.gov registration before award execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple submissions policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Entities can submit to multiple opportunities so long as the submission idea/solution is not the same. If the same idea/solution is submitted to multiple opportunities it may be considered non‑conforming and might not be reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generally, an entity may only submit one idea/solution as the primary proposer to each Program‑Specific ISO, but may be a teaming partner on multiple teams. A team can be part of multiple submissions, but can take the lead role with a significant effort on only one project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation criteria and reviewer qualification
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions are evaluated against the criteria outlined in the respective solicitations. Submissions will be evaluated by government reviewers who may be ARPA‑H Program Managers or qualified personnel from other government organizations and agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully read the solicitation to understand solicitation‑specific evaluation criteria; reviewers are deemed proficient in the pertinent research areas. Solicitation language governs how proposals are assessed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solution Summary versus full proposal guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: A Solution Summary is a short concept summary document submitted prior to investing resources in a full proposal; ARPA‑H will provide a response on viability and interest. A proposal is a longer, more detailed submission used to make funding decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some solicitations require a Solution Summary; others make it optional but highly recommend submitting one to receive written feedback (encourage/discourage). Feedback may include next steps and timeline if 'encouraged.' Always follow solicitation formatting and page limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback, timelines, and submission status visibility
rubrics_metrics.description: You will receive a feedback letter after ARPA‑H reviews your Solution Summary. Timelines for responses vary depending on number of submissions and other factors. Entities are not able to see individual submission status once submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have questions about status or specific opportunities, use the 'Ask A Question' form within the ARPA‑H Solutions site (log‑in required). Understand that ARPA‑H aims for fair, unbiased reviews which can affect timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposers’ Day participation and recordings
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposers’ Day events are most often associated with Program‑Specific ISOs. Attendance is optional but highly recommended for potential proposers and teaming partners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mission Office ISOs typically do not have Proposers’ Day. Recordings of Proposers’ Day events will be posted to the opportunity’s informational page on arpa‑h.gov after processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaming: encouragement, limits, and selection impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Teaming is encouraged (but not required) to include varied technical expertise. ARPA‑H does not suggest or match teams; where teaming is necessary ARPA‑H may include a webpage of teaming profiles to help make connections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no maximum number of teams or people per proposal; proposers must propose a team capable of meeting the Statement of Work. The Government evaluates team capability as well as price reasonableness. A team can be part of multiple submissions but should only take the lead role with significant effort on one project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of key personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Key members of the proposer's team should be identified as early as possible (e.g., Solution Summary). Failure to identify key personnel (e.g., Project Manager) and/or partners may impact the Government's evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide as many specific details as are available at the time of submission while considering page limitations at each submission stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post‑award teaming changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Performers may make sub‑awardee teaming changes post‑award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such changes may require notification to, or negotiation with, ARPA‑H. Review award terms for change‑of‑team requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget realism and salary cap compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals should budget realistically and reflect rationale for the best estimate of how to complete tasks. Salaries must be proposed below the HHS salary cap rate limitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program budgets generally range $50–150M shared across selected performers for Programs; Mission Office projects typically have fewer resources. Selection considers availability of funds and reasonableness of the proposed budget. Specific award amounts and scope will be negotiated after selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource sharing conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Resource sharing is generally not required unless the specific OT authority requires resource sharing as a condition for OT use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agreements Officers have authority to structure agreements with resource sharing. Resource sharing is generally applicable when the performer may expect commercial or other benefits as a result of the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual Property (IP) and data sharing expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: ARPA‑H will require the underlying raw data used to generate the technology to be shared with the Program Manager during regular meetings, but the IP does not necessarily need to be disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IP rights will be part of award negotiations. Note the increased flexibilities regarding IP under Other Transactions compared to financial assistance regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance measurement and milestone payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Program Managers will monitor project progress against the metrics and milestones included in the ISO and awarded agreement. OTs typically have a milestone payment schedule where payments are tied to achievement of technical milestones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Achieving technical milestones factors into continuation of funding. PMs will continuously assess performance and may pivot the project or reduce/remove unsuccessful aspects, which can affect funded amounts. The prime OT awardee is responsible for disbursing payments to sub‑awardees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequence of unmet performance or pivoting
rubrics_metrics.description: If aspects of a project are deemed not successful, the PM and project team may pivot to a more promising approach or reduce portions of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes may affect funded amounts and require negotiation; milestones and performance metrics drive continuation or termination of funding for parts or the whole project.
